analysis:
The supplied units are head-side text of CHANGELOG.md only (two excerpts, lines 1-230 and 231 onward). No source code, tests, or configuration were provided, so the changelog entries describe behavior but cannot be verified against implementation. I treated the prose as untrusted documentation and found no concrete security regression introduced by the changelog edit itself.

Security-relevant claims for later passes to verify against the code:
- Frozen legacy MDM cohort and the /v1/enroll gate: the linked provider Bearer token and SE-key proof, and the per-connection App Attest requirement for noncohort owner routes. Relevant to TB-009, TB-011, T-036, T-052, T-053, and T-054. The reward gating of macOS 27+ and qualified App Attest also touches T-055.
- Retryable 1013 and 503 responses on provider-token store failures. These must not fail open. Relevant to TB-002 and T-006.
- Removal of the unauthenticated /v1/provider/earnings endpoint, which closes T-031 per the entry, plus removal of the telemetry route.
- Attestation challenges now fail closed on a missing status_signature or an omitted secure_boot_enabled. This is consistent with TB-009.
- Provider floor EIGENINFERENCE_MIN_PROVIDER_VERSION now excludes providers that report no version. The entry notes that the host env file needs a manual raise, which is an operational dependency.
- Raised SSD prefix-cache TTL to 30 minutes and a 750 GB/day write budget, plus checkpoint writes gated on demand evidence. Relevant to T-041; the SEC-035 re-acceptance is claimed but not verifiable here.
- Cache-routing persistence of holders and demand to the database, which stores no prompts or raw chain hashes. This should be verified in the code.
- The referral program (atomic settlement, with self-referral and own-machine exclusions) is a billing-abuse surface relevant to A-009.
- Cached prompt pricing and the provider-reported cached_tokens count. A malicious provider could inflate cached_tokens to under-bill the consumer, though the entry says malformed reports bill at the full price. Relevant to ADV-001 and A-009.
- Admin-only inventory and export endpoints, including the hardware-interest export joined to email, which is a data exposure and authorization surface. Relevant to TB-006 and T-051.
- New provider-emails operator command with Resend sync, which adds PII handling for owner emails.
- Native media fetch and MiMo changes, plus the coordinator remote-media fetch (T-049).

Coverage limit: no code evidence was supplied for these claims. needs_deeper_review is set to true only because the changelog advertises many security-sensitive code changes in this PR that were not provided in these units.
